overviewHtml:
This graded quiz assesses your understanding of the French and German thinkers who prepared the ground for Merleau-Ponty's phenomenology of the body. You'll be asked about Bergson's duration, Gestalt and organismic challenges to atomism, and Sartre's and Beauvoir's accounts of the body.

Note: Aim for a score of 80 percent or higher. If you score lower, use the feedback to review the topics you missed, then retake the quiz.

forms.stemHtml: A growing sense of dread colors more and more of a person's thoughts until it is part of everything. What kind of multiplicity does Bergson say this is?

options.html: Quantitative, since it grows in amount
options.text: Quantitative, since it grows in amount
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on quantitative and qualitative multiplicity.

options.html: Qualitative, since its states interpenetrate
options.text: Qualitative, since its states interpenetrate
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A deepening feeling changes in quality and colors the others. It can't be counted without distortion.

options.html: Spatial, since it spreads across the mind
options.text: Spatial, since it spreads across the mind
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on quantitative and qualitative multiplicity.

options.html: Numerical, since each thought is a unit
options.text: Numerical, since each thought is a unit
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on quantitative and qualitative multiplicity.

forms.stemHtml: Bergson and Husserl both reject the idea that experience is a series of instants. Where do they differ most deeply?

options.html: Over whether time really exists at all
options.text: Over whether time really exists at all
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Bergson and Husserl on time.

options.html: Over whether memory of the past is possible
options.text: Over whether memory of the past is possible
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Bergson and Husserl on time.

options.html: Over whether analyzing time spatializes it
options.text: Over whether analyzing time spatializes it
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Husserl describes the present as a structure of phases. Bergson would suspect that such analysis begins to lay time out in space.

options.html: Over whether clocks measure time accurately
options.text: Over whether clocks measure time accurately
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Bergson and Husserl on time.

forms.stemHtml: What is Bergson's term for a multiplicity of states that interpenetrate and can't be counted, because each colors the others? Enter two words.

options.html: qualitative multiplicity
options.text: qualitative multiplicity
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Qualitative multiplicity contrasts with quantitative multiplicity, which is countable.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on quantitative and qualitative multiplicity.

forms.stemHtml: Why did Wertheimer's phi phenomenon challenge elementism?

options.html: Because observers couldn't see the two lines at all
options.text: Because observers couldn't see the two lines at all
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on elementism and the phi phenomenon.

options.html: Because seen motion matched no local stimulus
options.text: Because seen motion matched no local stimulus
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Only two stationary stimuli were shown, yet observers saw motion, which can't be a sensation in the elementist's sense.

options.html: Because the lines moved faster than the eye could track
options.text: Because the lines moved faster than the eye could track
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on elementism and the phi phenomenon.

options.html: Because each line produced two separate sensations
options.text: Because each line produced two separate sensations
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on elementism and the phi phenomenon.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following are consistent with Goldstein's holism? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: A symptom expresses the whole organism's reorganized response
options.text: A symptom expresses the whole organism's reorganized response
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! For Goldstein, symptoms must be understood through the organism's overall relation to its milieu.

options.html: An injured organism may narrow its milieu to what it can manage
options.text: An injured organism may narrow its milieu to what it can manage
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Goldstein observed that patients protect themselves by keeping their world small and predictable.

options.html: Each symptom reflects the loss of one isolated function
options.text: Each symptom reflects the loss of one isolated function
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Goldstein's holism.

options.html: Perception is assembled from independent local sensations
options.text: Perception is assembled from independent local sensations
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on elementism and the constancy hypothesis.

forms.stemHtml: In the row "xx xx xx", you see three pairs rather than six marks. Which Gestalt grouping principle explains this? Enter one word.

options.html: proximity
options.text: proximity
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Elements close together are seen as belonging together.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on figure–ground and grouping principles.

options.html: Because it's an object for consciousness

options.html: Because it's the source of every act

options.html: Because it's the true self behind the body
options.text: Because it's the true self behind the body
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Sartre's non-egological consciousness.

options.html: Because shame is learned from other people
options.text: Because shame is learned from other people

options.html: Because shame shows on the face for others to see
options.text: Because shame shows on the face for others to see

forms.stemHtml: What does Beauvoir mean in saying the body is "not a thing but a situation"?

options.html: That the body has no material reality at all
options.text: That the body has no material reality at all
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the body as situation and becoming a woman.

options.html: That its meaning depends on how it's lived
options.text: That its meaning depends on how it's lived
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Biological facts are real but not destiny. Their significance depends on the projects and social world in which the body is lived.

options.html: That the body is fully determined by biology
options.text: That the body is fully determined by biology
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the body as situation and becoming a woman.

options.html: That the body is a cultural layer on nature
options.text: That the body is a cultural layer on nature
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the body as situation and becoming a woman.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following are claims Beauvoir makes in The Ethics of Ambiguity? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Freedom is always exercised within a situation
options.text: Freedom is always exercised within a situation
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! For Beauvoir, freedom is situated.

options.html: Oppression is a limit on freedom imposed by others
options.text: Oppression is a limit on freedom imposed by others
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Oppression cuts a person off from their possibilities.

options.html: One can't will oneself free without willing others free
options.text: One can't will oneself free without willing others free
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! My freedom needs a world of free others to be realized.

options.html: Freedom is absolute, whatever the situation
options.text: Freedom is absolute, whatever the situation
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Beauvoir's ethics of ambiguity.

options.html: Human existence is purely a free subject
options.text: Human existence is purely a free subject
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Beauvoir's ethics of ambiguity.

forms.stemHtml: Why does Bergson call homogeneous, measured time "space in disguise"?

options.html: Because clocks are physical objects located in space
options.text: Because clocks are physical objects located in space
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on duration and spatialized time.

options.html: Because physics has shown that time is a dimension of space
options.text: Because physics has shown that time is a dimension of space
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on duration and spatialized time.

options.html: Because measuring lays moments out side by side as units
options.text: Because measuring lays moments out side by side as units
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Measuring time counts moments as distinct, identical units, which requires setting them out in space.

options.html: Because lived time can only be experienced while moving
options.text: Because lived time can only be experienced while moving
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on duration and spatialized time.

forms.stemHtml: What does Bergson mean by a free act?

options.html: An act with no cause of any kind
options.text: An act with no cause of any kind
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on duration, spatialized time, and free acts.

options.html: An act chosen after weighing each option
options.text: An act chosen after weighing each option
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on duration, spatialized time, and free acts.

options.html: An act that expresses the whole self in duration
options.text: An act that expresses the whole self in duration
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A free act springs from the whole personality, rather than from one prior state.

options.html: An act that follows a rule the agent chose
options.text: An act that follows a rule the agent chose
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on duration, spatialized time, and free acts.

forms.stemHtml: What is Bergson's term for time represented as a line of distinct, homogeneous moments laid side by side, as in clock time? Enter two words.

options.html: spatialized time
options.text: spatialized time
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Bergson calls spatialized time space in disguise.

options.html: spatialised time
options.text: spatialised time
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Bergson calls spatialized time space in disguise.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on duration and spatialized time.

forms.stemHtml: What was Köhler's main objection to the way elementists defended the constancy hypothesis?

options.html: It relied on experiments with animals
options.text: It relied on experiments with animals

options.html: It ignored differences in sense organs
options.text: It ignored differences in sense organs

options.html: It explained away contrary experience
options.text: It explained away contrary experience

options.html: It overestimated the role of attention
options.text: It overestimated the role of attention

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following would Goldstein classify as expressions of the abstract attitude? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Pretending to catch a ball that isn't there
options.text: Pretending to catch a ball that isn't there
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Acting on the merely possible requires detaching from the immediate situation.

options.html: Pointing to your knee because someone asked
options.text: Pointing to your knee because someone asked
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Acting on command is a mark of the abstract attitude.

options.html: Sorting objects by a rule you've chosen
options.text: Sorting objects by a rule you've chosen
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Shifting deliberately between aspects of a situation is part of the abstract attitude.

options.html: Swatting a fly that lands on your arm
options.text: Swatting a fly that lands on your arm
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Goldstein's holism and the two attitudes.

options.html: Catching a ball thrown straight to you
options.text: Catching a ball thrown straight to you
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Goldstein's holism and the two attitudes.

forms.stemHtml: A circle drawn with small gaps in its outline is still seen as a circle, not as a set of separate arcs. Which Gestalt grouping principle explains this? Enter one word.

options.html: closure
options.text: closure
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Elements that form a closed or nearly closed shape are seen as a unit.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on figure–ground and grouping principles.

forms.stemHtml: Counting coins, someone asks what you're doing, and you answer "counting" at once, without having reflected. What does this show, for Sartre?

options.html: That you were reflecting on yourself all along
options.text: That you were reflecting on yourself all along

options.html: That counting is an unconscious activity
options.text: That counting is an unconscious activity
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Sartre's non-egological consciousness.

options.html: That you had non-positional self-awareness
options.text: That you had non-positional self-awareness
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Consciousness was aware of itself implicitly, without positing itself as an object.

options.html: That the ego was present in your consciousness
options.text: That the ego was present in your consciousness
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on Sartre's non-egological consciousness.

forms.stemHtml: A job candidate feels her hands become awkward and conspicuous as the interview panel watches her. Which of Sartre's dimensions of the body is most present?

options.html: The body lived, passed over in silence
options.text: The body lived, passed over in silence

options.text: The body as an object for scientific study

options.html: My body as I exist it as known by others
options.text: My body as I exist it as known by others
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The third dimension is the body lived through the other's look, felt as exposed and alienated.

options.html: The body as extended substance
options.text: The body as extended substance

forms.stemHtml: How does Moi argue that Beauvoir's idea of the body as situation relates to the sex/gender distinction?

options.html: It makes the distinction unnecessary
options.text: It makes the distinction unnecessary

options.html: It reduces gender to biological sex
options.text: It reduces gender to biological sex

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following describe Sartre's rather than Beauvoir's position? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: It records every detail of the environment equally

options.html: It stores each past event as a unique memory image
options.text: It stores each past event as a unique memory image

forms.stemHtml: Why did Bergson's reputation decline from the 1920s on?

options.html: His books went out of print and were forgotten
options.text: His books went out of print and were forgotten

options.html: French philosophers turned to Husserl and Heidegger
options.text: French philosophers turned to Husserl and Heidegger
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A new generation found phenomenology more rigorous, and Bergson's vocabulary vague. His 1922 debate with Einstein didn't help.

options.html: He renounced his theory of duration in later work

options.html: Merleau-Ponty wrote a decisive refutation of him

forms.stemHtml: You remember one particular afternoon when you first read a poem: where you were and how the light fell. What is Bergson's term for this form of memory? Enter two words.

options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Pure memory records each past event as a unique, dated image, recalled rather than repeated.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following are concerns that critics have raised about the Schneider case? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Extensive testing may have shaped his performance

options.html: Later examiners didn't find the same pattern
options.text: Later examiners didn't find the same pattern
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Critics report that later examinations didn't replicate the original findings.

options.html: The reports mixed observation and interpretation
options.text: The reports mixed observation and interpretation
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This makes it harder to judge how far the evidence supports the conclusions.

options.html: The patient had never been injured at all
options.text: The patient had never been injured at all
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the Schneider case and its reliability.

options.html: The case was invented by Merleau-Ponty
options.text: The case was invented by Merleau-Ponty
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the Schneider case and its reliability.

forms.stemHtml: What is Goldstein's term for the capacity to detach from the immediate situation: to consider the merely possible, shift deliberately between aspects, and act on command? Enter two words.

options.text: The for-itself is never simply what it is
